topic.title: Lac-Mégantic: a parked oil train with too few hand brakes rolled away once its locomotive's engine was shut down after a fire

title: How Did a Train With No One Aboard Reach Lac-Mégantic?
description:
How did a train with no one aboard reach Lac-Mégantic at full speed?
It was parked on a hill for the night. We rebuild it in 3D: the hand brakes, the brake test, the fire, and the air that slowly leaked away.
Sources: TSB, TSB news release (Aug 2014).
Based on official investigation reports and published sources. 3D scenes are reconstructions, not actual footage.
cta: Hand brakes or the brake test: which should have stopped it? Comment

topic.title: One Phone Call Doubled the Load on This Walkway

title: The Hyatt Walkway Collapse: One Phone Call Doubled the Load
description:
In Kansas City, two steel walkways hung above a crowded hotel atrium on thin rods. Why did they fall?
This is the full cause chain from the federal investigation: a connection that was already too weak, a change agreed by phone during construction, a connection that nobody calculated, and the nut that pulled through its beam.
Then what the investigators measured in their lab, and the rule every engineer works under because of it.

CHAPTERS
0:00 The walkways and the question
0:44 The hotel
1:35 How it was meant to hold
2:41 The chain
4:47 The last minutes
5:31 The failure
6:36 What the investigators found
7:37 What changed

Sources: National Bureau of Standards, Investigation of the Kansas City Hyatt Regency Walkways Collapse; ASCE Civil Engineering magazine.
Based on official investigation reports and published sources. 3D scenes are reconstructions, not actual footage.

Report: US National Institute of Standards and Technology, nbsbuildingscience143, page 7 of 378, Public domain (US government work) (https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/BSS/nbsbuildingscience143.pdf)

topic.title: New Orleans: a tanker's rudder jammed on the Mississippi and two minutes later it hit a docked riverboat, which capsized in 22 minutes (NTSB, preliminary)

title: Why Couldn't This Mississippi Tanker Stop?
description:
Why couldn't a tanker on the Mississippi at New Orleans stop before it hit a docked riverboat?
Its rudder jammed. We reconstruct it in 3D from the NTSB's preliminary information: the stuck rudder, why a ship can't brake, the riverboat. The cause of the jam is still under investigation.
Sources: NTSB, AP (Nov 2026).
Based on official investigation reports and published sources. 3D scenes are reconstructions, not actual footage.
cta: The fast hit or the slow capsize: which surprised you more? Comment

topic.title: The Gauge Said Normal. The Tower Was Nearly Full.

title: The Gauge Said Normal. The Tower Was Nearly Full.
description:
One March morning a distillation tower at the BP Texas City refinery was started up after maintenance. Its level gauge said the liquid was low. It was nearly at the top.
We rebuild the unit in 3D and follow the U.S. Chemical Safety Board's investigation: a tower filled for hours with nothing taken out, a gauge that could only see the bottom of it, an old vent stack with no flare, and trailers parked close by.
Then what the board found, and what it asked the industry to change.

CHAPTERS
0:00 Intro
0:41 The Unit
1:42 The Start-up
2:56 The Gauge
3:47 The Overflow
5:02 The Blast
6:03 The Findings
7:04 What Changed

Source: U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board, Refinery Explosion and Fire, BP Texas City (final report).
Based on official investigation reports and published sources. 3D scenes are reconstructions, not actual footage.

Report: US Chemical Safety Board, CSB Investigation Report: Refinery Explosion and Fire, BP Texas City, page 18 of 341, Public domain (US government work) (https://www.csb.gov/assets/1/20/CSBFinalReportBP.pdf?13841)
Report: US Chemical Safety Board, CSB Investigation Report: Refinery Explosion and Fire, BP Texas City, page 24 of 341, Public domain (US government work) (https://www.csb.gov/assets/1/20/CSBFinalReportBP.pdf?13841)

topic.title: Calabasas, 2020: why the NTSB says a helicopter climbing out of cloud was already turning the wrong way (Kobe Bryant's flight, NTSB AAR-21/01)

title: Kobe Bryant's Helicopter: Why Did the Pilot Think He Was Climbing?
description:
In thick cloud over Calabasas, Kobe Bryant's pilot said he was climbing. What was the helicopter really doing?
We reconstruct the flight in 3D from the NTSB's final report: the climb into cloud, how the inner ear stops sensing a steady turn, and the recommendations that followed.
Sources: NTSB (Feb 2021).
Based on official investigation reports and published sources. 3D scenes are reconstructions, not actual footage.
cta: Your body or the instruments: which would you trust in cloud? Comment
